data.name: Protect your planet
data.detailed_description:
Did you ever want to have your own planet or an asteroid? Protect your planet will give you this opportunity, but you will have to protect your planet from an asteroids storm. Destroy huge asteroids by clicking on them to save the life of your planet!

Use boosters to more effectively destroy asteroids and save the lives of your planet!

Featuring:

- Beautiful, full resolution graphics and design
- Control over time management by the boosters!
- Frequent feature updates, including new boosters!
- Infinite Gameplay: Even when you think it ends, there's more!

Planned features:


-Full featured Leaderboard system

Start defending your first planet!
Thanks for playing Protect your planet!

reviews.review:
Protect your planet is a compact arcade-style planetary defense game that turns a very simple concept into an endless test of attention and reaction speed. Developed and published by Triple Rush Games, it places the player in charge of protecting a vulnerable celestial body from incoming asteroids. Rather than introducing complicated controls or layers of strategic management, the game focuses on immediate interaction: identify approaching threats and eliminate them before they collide with the planet. This simplicity makes the experience approachable within moments of starting, although it also means that players should expect a relatively narrow gameplay loop.

The core action revolves around clicking incoming asteroids to destroy them. It is an uncomplicated mechanic, but the challenge emerges when several threats begin demanding attention at the same time. Players need to watch different areas surrounding the planet, recognize which asteroids pose the most immediate danger, and react quickly enough to prevent collisions. There is an arcade-like satisfaction to successfully clearing a dangerous wave, especially when the situation briefly appears overwhelming. The controls are therefore less about mechanical complexity and more about maintaining concentration and responding efficiently under pressure.

Boosters add another element to the otherwise straightforward formula. These provide additional assistance when ordinary clicking is no longer sufficient to comfortably manage the incoming hazards. Their presence gives players something beyond pure reaction speed to consider, since using additional capabilities at appropriate moments can help recover from increasingly difficult situations. The system does not transform the game into a deep strategy experience, but it gives the defensive loop some welcome variation and prevents every moment from depending exclusively on repetitive clicking.

One of the defining characteristics of the game is its endless structure. Instead of progressing through a conventional campaign with missions, characters, or a final objective, the experience is primarily about surviving for as long as possible. This approach is well suited to short arcade sessions because players can quickly enter the action, attempt to improve their performance, and stop whenever they have had enough. The disadvantage is that endless gameplay does not automatically provide endless variety. Once the fundamental mechanics have been learned, repetition becomes increasingly noticeable, particularly during extended sessions.

The presentation follows the same minimalist philosophy as the gameplay. Its space setting provides an immediately understandable backdrop for the asteroid-defense premise, while the relatively uncluttered presentation helps players identify incoming objects without excessive visual distraction. It is functional rather than spectacular, placing readability ahead of elaborate environmental detail or cinematic presentation. Players attracted to visually ambitious space games will find little comparable spectacle here, but the graphics are appropriate for a modest reaction-focused arcade title.

There is also little narrative material competing for attention. The planet itself is essentially the objective that gives the player's actions purpose rather than the centerpiece of an elaborate story. This makes the game easy to approach for anyone who simply wants immediate gameplay without dialogue, cutscenes, lengthy tutorials, or complicated world-building. At the same time, the absence of a stronger narrative or broader progression system reduces the sense of long-term investment. Players motivated by unlocking extensive content, developing characters, exploring environments, or completing a structured campaign are unlikely to find those motivations here.

The game's greatest strength is accessibility. The basic objective can be understood almost immediately, making it suitable for players who enjoy uncomplicated arcade challenges. There is very little friction between launching the game and engaging with its main mechanic. Short sessions can be enjoyable because the experience does not require players to remember complicated systems between playthroughs. It is the kind of design where reaction speed and personal improvement can provide much of the motivation.

Its greatest weakness is consequently its limited depth. Repeatedly destroying asteroids can become predictable once the initial novelty disappears. Increasing pressure makes survival harder, but greater difficulty does not necessarily introduce fundamentally different gameplay. Players who enjoy chasing better performances or surviving increasingly intense situations may appreciate this focused design, while anyone who expects substantial mechanical evolution is more likely to feel that the experience runs out of fresh ideas relatively quickly.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially rated by Valve as Verified or Playable for this title. The game was primarily designed around Windows and mouse-based interaction, with clicking forming an important part of its gameplay. It may potentially be launched through Steam Deck's Proton compatibility layer, and the Deck's trackpads or touchscreen could theoretically accommodate its pointer-oriented controls, but this should not be interpreted as guaranteed compatibility. Without an official Steam Deck compatibility rating, players should consider it unsupported or unverified rather than assuming a completely trouble-free handheld experience.

Overall, Protect your planet works best as a modest arcade diversion rather than a deep planetary defense simulation. Its straightforward controls, instantly recognizable objective, boosters, and endless survival structure make it easy to understand and suitable for brief sessions. The tradeoff is substantial repetition and limited mechanical variety, so its lasting appeal depends heavily on how much the player enjoys simple reaction-based challenges. It accomplishes its basic purpose competently but lacks the breadth and progression necessary to become a particularly memorable long-term experience.

Rating: 5/10
